flashcard_questions.q: When was A Christmas Carol published?
Which 1834 law made the workhouse the main form of relief for the poor?
Which economist's ideas lie behind Scrooge's ‘surplus population’ remark?
Which single line acts as the thesis statement of the whole novella?
Which family represents the ‘deserving poor’ in the novella?
What does Dickens argue poverty is, rather than a moral failing?
flashcard_questions.a: A systemic injustice perpetuated by the wealthy.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the five-stave structure of the novella imitate?
flashcard_questions.a: A Christmas carol — a song in five parts.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the rising fearfulness of the three ghosts mirror?
What does the shift from darkness to golden sunlight track?
flashcard_questions.a: Scrooge's progress from selfishness to generosity.

flashcard_questions.q: Which narrative technique makes Dickens's moral message feel personal?
flashcard_questions.a: Direct address, with the narrator speaking straight to the reader.

flashcard_questions.q: Which closing line pulls the reader into Tiny Tim's blessing?
Which literary tradition supplies the ghosts, graveyards and dread?
What work was Dickens sent to at the age of twelve?
What did Dickens read in 1843 that prompted him to write the novella?
flashcard_questions.a: A Parliamentary report on child labour.

flashcard_questions.q: Which metaphor does Fred use for what Christmas unlocks in people?

notes: 15 cards: 5 context-to-relevance (1843, the Poor Law, Malthus, the blacking factory, the child-labour report), 4 structure and form (five staves, rising ghost intensity, light-to-dark arc, direct address), 3 theme-to-quotation, 2 theme-to-argument, 1 genre card. Dropped social responsibility, redemption, imagery, pathetic fallacy, allegorical and ignorance as glossary cards — they are abstract labels the quotation cards already test, and several would interfere with one another in one deck.
